messages:
Priya: Noticed a steady uptick in client errors when customers send very wide vectors in big batches. Errors look like 413 + some 422s for malformed shapes. Thinking about an "adaptive byte-budget" layer that smooths client bursts and gives actionable guidance.
Gabe: Can you sketch what "adaptive byte-budget" means?
Priya: Idea: compute a soft per-request byte budget based on tenant historical avg vector_size and a global max. If request > budget, return a lightweight estimate response (not full preflight) that includes a suggested `X-Embed-Unit-Estimate` header clients can use to decide.
Linh: I like lightweight over full preflight. Full preflight is heavier because it may parse entire payload. Estimate header could be computed from Content-Length + dims header if present.
Maya: UX: console should surface "estimated units" per recent request and a time-series showing when adaptive budget was applied. Also allow toggling show_examples which would display a sample split plan.
Priya: Telemetry events: embed_adapt.estimate_shown, embed_adapt.enforced, embed_adapt.override_by_client. Tag with tenant_id, dims_hint, raw_bytes.
Gabe: Quotas: if units are our billing primitive, we need to ensure adaptive budget doesn't undercount. Proposal: billing uses actual processed vectors (post-split) but quota checks use the conservative estimate. So no one gets free tokens.
Linh: Edge-case: clients that omit dims header. We'll infer dims by sampling first vector and store a session hint. Add heuristic: if inferred dims deviates later, reject with 422 and include `explain: dims_inconsistent`.
Maya: Rollout: feature-flagged backend + console opt-in for tenants. Start with non-enforced advisory mode (only emits estimate header + telemetry) for 2 weeks, then flip to soft-enforce (return 413 + estimate) for 5% traffic.
Priya: Implementation notes: estimator = min(global_max_bytes, tenant_percentile(95, historical_bytes_per_vector) * vectors + overhead). Cache per (tenant, dims_hint) with TTL 10m.
Gabe: Runtime perf: keep estimator path in front of parser to avoid decoding huge JSON. Use Content-Length + first-chunk peek to infer dims without buffering whole body.
Linh: Security: ensure estimate responses do not echo vector content. Return only aggregates and safe hints. Matches data retention policy.
Maya: Console: add "What happened" flyout when a request triggered enforcement showing guidance: "Reduce batch size to N, or send dims header X" and quick curl to split client-side. Also show cost delta if they used server-split vs client-split.
Priya: Ops: alerting - OpsBot create a new alert when adaptive_enforced_rate > 1% over 10m.
OpsBot: Alert created: adaptive_enforced_rate > 1% over 10m on /v1/embeddings -> paging eng-sre.
Gabe: Example logs from a local canary:
`2026-03-20T03:14:09Z embed_adapt: estimate tenant=acme dims_hint=1536 orig_bytes=18600000 est_units=2760 mode=advisory`
`2026-03-20T03:14:09Z embed_adapt: enforced tenant=acme orig_bytes=18600000 action=reject est_header=2760`
Linh: API suggestion: support header `X-Embed-Dims` and `X-Embed-Estimate-Only: true` to let SDKs opt into advisory mode. Response when advisory: `200 {"estimate_units":2760, "suggested_max_batch": 1200, "explainability":["wide_vectors","large_batch"]}`
Maya: Billing follow-up: product asked whether advisory estimates should count against burst quotas. We think advisory = no, enforced = yes. Need product + billing signoff.
Priya: Canaries: start in advisory globally for 7 days, then canary enforced to 5% traffic with `allow_server_split` false by default. Provide tenant opt-in `allow_server_split=true`.
Gabe: Client SDK work: add fast-fail client that checks server estimate header and splits before sending if header < intended_units. We'll update Node/Python SDKs.
Linh: Testing: fuzz tests for mixed-dim arrays and a bench to ensure estimate path adds <1ms median overhead.
Maya: Console KPI panel: estimate_rate, enforced_rate, avg_estimate_vs_actual_ratio, preflight_cache_hit_rate.
Priya: Next steps: I'll open RFC with the estimator formula + caching strategy. Gabe will prototype header plumbing. Linh will add infer-dims peek implementation. Maya will mock Console panels. OpsBot: create a canary runbook snippet.
OpsBot: Runbook entry created: Adaptive Byte Budget canary -> steps: enable advisory flag, monitor metrics, rollback if enforced_rate > 2% or error_increase > 0.5%.
